nightly-harness: CI nightly-run finished: eval-suite v3.1 on model q4_0 failed 23/300 prompts (7.6%), 9 timeouts, spikes in nondet bad generations. attaching summary link: https://ci/redwood/nightly/2003456789 :eyes:
will: saw the alert, jumping in. which prompt set?
sam: persona-bias-2026 (the usual long-form prompts). failures are clustered near prompt indices 120-140.
eva: saw similar pattern yesterday but chalked it up to infra noise. logs show repeated 'TokenizerError: inconsistent ids' then timeouts.
will: log excerpt:
```
ERROR EvaluationWorker: prompt_idx=127 model=q4_0: TokenizerError: token ids mismatch for same input
  at tokenizer._encode (tokenizer.py:312)
  at eval_runner.py:98
TimeoutError: Eval timed out after 30.0s (while waiting for response)
```
will: that TokenizerError is weird — suggests nondeterminism at tokenization stage rather than sampling.
sam: search shows one commit last week that added a mutable tokenizer cache to speed repeated encodings (`tokenizer._fast_cache`). might be correlated.
eva: here's the suspicious code from the harness (snippet):
```
# naive cache introduced to speed batch tokenization
if not hasattr(tokenizer, "_fast_cache"):
    tokenizer._fast_cache = {}
key = (text, model_variant)
if key in tokenizer._fast_cache:
    return tokenizer._fast_cache[key]
# mutate global cache while concurrently used by other threads
token_ids = tokenizer._unsafe_encode(text)
tokenizer._fast_cache[key] = token_ids
return token_ids
```
eva: race: two threads encode same text, one writes partial state, other reads -> inconsistent ids. plus cache items reused across quantized/FP variants causing tokenization divergence.
will: that matches stacktrace: inconsistent ids for same input across consecutive runs. could also explain timeouts when downstream code gets bad token shapes.
sam: quick repro idea: run 20 parallel encodes of same long prompt against q4_0 harness with the cache enabled. if flaky, toggling to per-thread cache or locking should fix.
eva: I repro locally with a small script, flakiness goes away when I replace `_fast_cache` with `threading.local()` or add a lock.
will: nice. can we fix in harness quickly? prefer add a simple lock around cache writes to avoid perf regress until proper LRU thread-safe cache is implemented.
ci-bot: @will opened PR #4782 applied a conservative fix (mutex around cache writes) and added stress test (parallel_tokenize_fuzz) to nightly.
will: deployed PR to staging harness, kicked off nightly job. staging run passed 300/300, 0 timeouts. :lock:
will: follow-up items — plan: 1) replace naive dict with a concurrent cache (LRU) 2) add tokenization determinism unit tests across quantized variants 3) audit other places that mutate tokenizer objects at runtime.
sam: I'll file the follow-up GH issues and assign — also add a note in the model-onboarding checklist to avoid adding global mutable state to tokenizer wrappers.
eva: adding a changelog entry for the harness fix. will monitor next 3 nights.
nightly-harness: scheduled 3-night observation window starting now. will post aggregate if regressions reappear.
will: thanks all. big win — looks like infra nondet, not model regression. :tada:
